criteria.criterion: The change description names the root cause: the guard infers the stop reason from free-text closing-reason prefixes and has two disagreeing environment lists, so an auth-expiry stop counted as line spend; the fix is in the shared classifier in crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs and scope_guard.rs, not in one job's data.
criteria.evidence: Read in `git diff HEAD~1`. The CHANGELOG.md Fixed entry, the doc comment on `StopCause` in disk.rs and the module doc of scope_guard.rs all name the cause the same way. The guard read a free-text `environment:` prefix, while `is_environment_reason` listed only low disk and check timeout. So `the producer did not complete: ...` for a 401 error matched neither list and counted as work, and the stored pause was never checked again. The fix is `disk::StopCause::of`, used by `scope_guard::verdict_of` and `resumable_stop`, plus the pause recompute in `line_pause`. No job data is touched.
commands: git diff HEAD~1 -- CHANGELOG.md crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs crates/athena-core/src/status.rs

criteria.criterion: `scope_guard::attempt_of` and `disk::is_environment_reason`/`resumable_stop` use one classifier (no second hard-coded list); Grep shows a single definition of which closing reasons are environment stops.
criteria.evidence: Grep under crates/ for `ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX`, `starts_with("environment` and `StopCause::of`: the constant is defined once, in disk.rs:263, and used only in disk.rs. scope_guard.rs:547 (`verdict_of`, which `attempt_of` calls) goes through `crate::disk::is_environment_reason`, and that function is `StopCause::of(reason).is_environment()`. `resumable_stop` and run/mod.rs:594 call the same function. The guard's old `ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX` constant is removed. `disk::tests::one_classifier_decides_environment_reasons` passed.

findings.summary: The 401 and 429 classification still parses the CLI's error text (`API Error: NNN` after a `success: ` or `error: ` subtype) instead of a typed outcome from the agent driver.
findings.evidence: `api_error_status` in disk.rs reads the status from the `detail` string that `output_from_result` builds. It is tied to a fixed position and tested through the real stream parser, so it does not match common words. But if the CLI changes this wording, these stops quietly count as work again. The sturdier fix is for athena-agent to report a structured API-error status in `InvocationOutcome` or the record. That is outside this reading's 'no new record schema' assumption, so it is minor.

findings.summary: `line_pause` returns the stored mark's text even when the recomputed pause rests on different signals.
findings.evidence: `line_pause` checks only `overall() == Level::Pause` and then returns the stored mark. A stored T4 pause on a line that now pauses for T5 would show the T4 refusal text.

summary: The change fixes the root cause where it starts. Before, the scope guard read a free-text `environment:` prefix while `disk::is_environment_reason` kept a second, shorter list, so a producer stop on an expired login (401) counted as spend on the line. Now there is one classifier, `disk::StopCause::of`, used by both the guard (`scope_guard::verdict_of`) and `athena retry` (`resumable_stop`). The producer now closes 401 and 429 errors with an `environment:` reason, and older unprefixed records are still read correctly. `line_pause` and `athena status` now recompute a line's signals from its attempts, so a stored pause that no longer holds stops blocking. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard` (33 passed) and `cargo test -p athena-core disk` (32 passed). The new tests cover an expired-login line raising no T1, T3 or T5 signal, each kind of environment stop, the TimedOut and work-failure controls, a stale pause being ignored while a real T4 or T3 pause still refuses, and expired-login stops being resumable. A grep shows the environment prefix is defined only in disk.rs. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs (1846 tests) passed. Every changed file is on the deliverables list, and no governance file changed. One minor point remains: the 401/429 detection reads the CLI's `API Error: NNN` text rather than a typed status from the agent driver.
